Three portals, one record

One advising file, read three different ways.

Row-level security decides what each role can see. Advising notes and attempt remarks never reach a student session — not by convention, by policy in the database.

For students

Open the checklist you were handed on paper — but current. See which slots are filled, which retake counts, and what the lapsed INC does to your GWA before the term ends.

  • Curriculum checklist with live slot status
  • Term and cumulative GWA, unit-weighted
  • Full attempt history across retakes
  • Your assigned adviser, always current

For advisers

Record the attempt, see the prerequisite warning, and decide — with the override written to an audit entry that nobody can quietly edit later.

  • Advisee roster with delinquency and INC alerts
  • Soft prerequisite check with Continue / Cancel
  • Elective mapping and transfer equivalency
  • Dated, append-only advising notes

For administrators

Own the catalog: programs, versioned curricula, prerequisite links, repeatable rules, term locks — and read the audit log the registrar will ask you for.

  • Provision accounts; no public sign-up
  • Versioned curricula with delinquency thresholds
  • School terms, offerings, by-request flags
  • Read-only immutable audit viewer

SAAIS keeps the whole advising office working from one file — so a student is never told two different things about the same requirement, and no decision has to be reconstructed from memory.

Confidence and clarity for the whole advising office, in one record.

The checklist resolves itself.

A slot is satisfied by a direct attempt, an equivalency decision, a discontinued-course equivalency, or an elective mapping. The checklist shows which — not just a tick.

Versioned curricula
Students stay bound to the curriculum version they entered under.
Positional vs. calendar terms
Year 1 / Term 1 is a slot; AY 2025–2026 1st Sem is a date.
Provenance on every slot
A filled slot names what filled it — attempt, equivalency or elective mapping — and who approved it.

The prerequisite engine

Warn the adviser. Never block the judgement.

Strict prerequisites are checked at enrollment, but SAAIS is a soft-check system: the adviser may continue, and the continuation is the thing that gets recorded.

Prerequisite not satisfied

[Student name] has not passed CS 121 Data Structures, a strict prerequisite of CS 132 Algorithms. Continuing records the attempt with prerequisite_override = true and writes an audit entry under your name.

What the build commits to

Aligned to RA 10173

Grades, enrollment records and advising notes are treated as sensitive personal information under the Philippine Data Privacy Act.

Built to WCAG 2.1 AA

Status is never colour alone; every badge carries a label and a shape. Full keyboard paths, including the override dialog. Audited in Phase 4.

Row-level security, append-only audit

Role boundaries live in the database, not in application discipline. The audit table rejects UPDATE and DELETE outright.

18

core entities modelled in the advising schema — the whole advising record, not a subset of it

1.00–5.00
grading scale, in discrete 0.25 steps
5
workflow phases from catalog to audit

gaps allowed in adviser continuity

From a name on a list to a signed audit entry.

3

Record

An attempt is bound to a course offering. Strict prerequisites soft-check; the adviser may continue, and the continuation is what gets written.

What this step writes
attempt
one row, bound to an offering in an unlocked school term
prerequisite_override
set true only when the adviser continues past the warning
audit entry
written in the same transaction, under the adviser's name
The rules engine

Every exception the registrar argues about, written down once.

These are not settings buried in a form. Each rule is a documented operation in the OpenAPI contract and a constraint in the database.

Repeatable types

grade_replacement keeps only the most recent passed attempt; additional_credit stacks every pass. A later failure never reverts a course already passed.

Lapsed INC recompute

A daily pg_cron job re-evaluates INCs past their one-year deadline, so a GWA changes with the calendar even when no row was edited.

Zero-gap reassignment

The incoming assignment starts the day the outgoing one ends — enforced in one transaction and backstopped by a database constraint.

Elective mapping

An adviser maps a real enrolled course into an open elective slot. The checklist shows actual units earned against the nominal slot.

Transfer equivalency

One-to-one decisions let a passed course from the old curriculum satisfy a destination slot without re-triggering a GWA recompute.

Term locks & by-request

Locked school terms refuse new attempts; by-request offerings stay visible to advisers without appearing as scheduled sections.

Roadmap

Delivered in five phases, not one big launch.

Phases 1 to 3 are built in the specification and the mockup set. Phases 4 and 5 are planned, and are drawn as planned — nothing here is deployed.

POST/functions/v1/enrollment-attempts

recordEnrollmentAttempt

Records a student attempt against a course offering. Runs the strict-prerequisite soft check. When prerequisite_override is true, the attempt and its AuditLogEntry are written in a single transaction.

bearerAuthRole: adviser, adminContract v1.4.0

Request body

Field Type Required Notes
student_id uuid yes Must be an actively assigned advisee.
course_offering_id uuid yes Offering must belong to an unlocked school term.
curriculum_term_course_id uuid no Set when the attempt fills a checklist slot.
prerequisite_override boolean no Defaults to false; true forces the audit write.
override_reason string conditional Required when the override flag is true.

Responses

201Attempt recorded.
409Strict prerequisite not satisfied and no override supplied.
403Caller is not the student's active adviser.
423The school term is locked.
Request 
POST /functions/v1/enrollment-attempts
Body 
{
  "student_id": "b7c1…9f2a",
  "course_offering_id": "3d40…11c8",
  "curriculum_term_course_id": "9a02…7b31",
  "prerequisite_override": true,
  "override_reason": "Concurrent with CS 121 retake; approved by dept chair."
}

How your GWA is computed

Sum of (final grade × units) divided by total units, across every counting attempt. A retake under grade replacement supersedes its earlier attempt; a course marked additional credit counts every passed attempt separately. Unresolved INCs past their deadline are evaluated as 5.00 without changing the recorded status.

Σ(grade × units) ÷ Σ units
102.50 ÷ 61 = 1.68

Three colors carried straight off the mark: the deep olive of the tile, the gold of the field, the cream of the letterform. Gold is the only accent and it is reserved — it marks the override, the exception, the thing an auditor will look for.

Status vocabulary

PassedFailedINCINC lapsedEnrolledDroppedNo attendanceNot taken

Every badge carries a text label as well as a color, and each pairs a dot with the word — color is never the only channel. INC and INC lapsed are deliberately distinct: a lapsed INC keeps the status it was given and is only evaluated as 5.00.

Contrast
All badge text clears 4.5:1 on its own ground.
Focus ring
2px forest outline, 2px offset, on every interactive element.
Hit target
44px minimum on touch surfaces.
Screen readers
Status is announced as text, not as a color name.

Buttons and controls

Gold is used for exactly one button in the product: Continue with override. Nothing else competes with it.

Search
Advisory — an exception the adviser should read before continuing.
Confirmed — the invariant held and the write is safe.
Blocked — the request was refused by a policy or a lock.

One stroke-based family on a 24px grid at 1.6 weight. No emoji anywhere in the product.
